statements.text: A UK government spokesperson said Ukraine has repeatedly shown it is serious about peace, while Russia has repeatedly rejected full and partial ceasefires and continues attacks on Ukrainian civilians and energy, and that Russia could end the war today.

A UK government spokesperson said the UK will keep working with international partners to ensure Ukraine has the military and financial support it needs, and will maintain pressure on Russia through what it called the toughest sanctions regime ever imposed by the UK.

The Prime Minister told the Commons the government's assessment is that the RAF Fairford incident is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard, and said the UK will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC's capacity to do harm.

The Prime Minister told the Commons he welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire, and said President Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed.

The Prime Minister will invite the First Minister to work with him on pushing more power out of Westminster and Holyrood, and will call on the Scottish Government to work with the UK Government through No10 North and the Scotland Office on a new model of regional empowerment. Douglas Alexander said the Prime Minister's offer is a genuine one and the Scotland Office is ready to help make it happen.

The Prime Minister is to offer Scotland a model of localised employment support similar to England's DWP devolution, shaped by Holyrood, and the National Economic Council is to meet the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales and the First Minister and Deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland in a couple of weeks to put the offer on the table.

The Prime Minister said the review led by Alan Milburn challenges the system to be built on the Easterhouse principle of names not numbers, and called for deeper devolution in Scotland to empower its places.
The Prime Minister said the Scottish government has agreed to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west.

The UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November, with a trade deal on food and drink, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration on the table. The Prime Minister said a food and drink deal is expected to add over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040.

The Prime Minister said he will work hard over the next five weeks to secure a deal at the summit, and believes the UK's chances will be enhanced by being open to discussing its longer-term relationship with the EU. He said he wants a serious dialogue on the options after the summit.

Ahead of President Zelenskyy's visit on 13 October, the government said the Prime Minister would tell him he has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages, and would accelerate delivery of air defence missiles, including British Lightweight Multirole Missiles against jet-powered drones.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK's rock-solid support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe, that it is not just the right thing but the necessary thing to do, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor John Healey will use meetings at the IMF in Bangkok to urge partners to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian LNG, and urged partners to back the ban to curtail the war chest funding Putin.

At Downing Street on 14 October the Prime Minister welcomed President Zelenskyy, and the leaders underlined that Russia had no interest in peace. The leaders discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support on long-range missiles ahead of the winter. The Prime Minister said the UK would keep developing innovative military solutions, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted by other partners, and would continue diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.

The Great British Railways headquarters is to be built at Becketwell in Derby, with construction expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, accommodating up to 450 GBR staff, with an estimated £151 million boost to the local economy. Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with the first starters based in Derby.

Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, and that she is delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home, bringing jobs, investment and opportunity to Derby.

Pat McFadden said the foundation apprenticeship forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn. Up to 600 apprentices will enrol over the next four years, with the first starters based in Derby.
The UK will take up the G20 presidency in 2027 with AI centre stage, and aims to work towards agreeing a single set of global principles and standards on AI during its presidency year.
